qs.q: Why are aminoglycosides completely ineffective when treating infections caused by obligate anaerobic bacteria?
qs.e: Aminoglycosides rely on an oxygen-dependent transport mechanism to cross the bacterial cell membrane, making them inactive against anaerobes. Their primary intracellular target is indeed the 30S ribosomal subunit.
